_note: Plain-language general meanings written by the LexLocal team. General information, not legal advice; how a term applies depends on the document and the law.
lock-in period: A period during which a party agrees not to end the agreement early.
indemnify: To promise to cover another party's losses or costs in certain situations.
indemnity: A promise to cover another party's losses or costs in certain situations.
force majeure: Events outside the parties' control (such as natural disasters) that may excuse a party from doing what it promised.
arbitration: Resolving a dispute through a private arbitrator instead of a court.
arbitrator: A private person chosen to decide a dispute instead of a judge.
jurisdiction: Which court or place has the authority to hear a dispute.
governing law: The law that will be used to interpret the agreement.
lessor: The owner who gives property on lease.
lessee: The person who takes property on lease.
licensor: The owner who gives permission to use a property under a leave-and-license agreement.
licensee: The person who is given permission to use a property under a leave-and-license agreement.
leave and license: An arrangement where the owner permits someone to use a property for a period without transferring a tenancy interest.
security deposit: Money paid up front and held as security, usually returned at the end after permitted deductions.
forfeit: To lose a right or money, usually as a consequence of breaking a condition.
forfeiture: Losing a right or money as a consequence of breaking a condition.
breach: Failing to do what the agreement requires.
material breach: A serious failure to perform the agreement, as opposed to a minor one.
notice period: The advance warning one party must give the other before ending the agreement or taking an action.
termination: Ending the agreement before or at the end of its term.
sublet: To rent all or part of a rented property to someone else.
assign: To transfer your rights under the agreement to someone else.
liquidated damages: An amount fixed in advance in the agreement to be paid if a particular breach happens.
waive: To give up a right voluntarily.
escalation: An agreed increase, for example in rent, at set times.
stamp duty: A tax paid on certain documents so that they are properly executed.
registration: Recording a document with a government office such as the sub-registrar.
probation: An initial period of employment during which performance is assessed, often with shorter notice.
confirmation: The point when an employee completes probation and becomes a regular employee.
cost to company: The total yearly cost of employing someone, which can include items that are not paid out monthly.
non-compete: A promise not to work for competitors or start a competing business for a period.
non-solicitation: A promise not to approach the other party's clients or employees for a period.
confidential information: Information the agreement says must be kept secret.
intellectual property: Creations of the mind such as inventions, software and designs, and the rights in them.
in lieu of notice: Paying money instead of giving the required notice period.
garden leave: A period where an employee is still employed and paid but is told not to work.
consideration: What each party gives or promises in exchange for what the other gives.
hereinafter: From this point on in the document.
whereas: Introduces background facts at the start of an agreement.
sole discretion: One party alone decides, without needing the other's agreement.
without prejudice: Without affecting a party's existing rights or claims.
vacant and peaceful possession: Handing over the property empty and without anyone else claiming it.
normal wear and tear: Ordinary deterioration from normal use, as opposed to damage.
